title: Admission bridge: batch translation, deterministic smoke, and empirical profile emitter
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an end-to-end admission bridge that reliably translates arbitrary community weights into Redwood runtime artifacts, runs a deterministic smoke suite, and emits an empirical performance profile that can be pinned and published. This ticket stitches together the translator, deterministic validator, and the profile emitter (a small microservice that produces kernel/latency/cost fingerprints and canonical pin metadata). The goal is to reduce manual triage for new OSS LLMs and make initial admission repeatable and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: Translator accepts at least three major OSS formats (PyTorch .pt, HF safetensors, and a simple GGML input) and produces a standardized runtime bundle with metadata headers.
Deterministic smoke suite executes on a canonical small prompt set and returns consistent outputs across two identical hardware types within allowed nondeterminism thresholds.

Empirical profile emitter uploads a profile artifact to the model catalog with fields: latency P50/P95, tokens/sec, KV-cache hit baseline, memory footprint at max-seqlen, and recommended quantization profile.
Automatic pin metadata (model version, conversion hash, compatible runtime kernels) is suggested and published to staging catalog for review via the onboarding UI.
Telemetry emitted follows telemetry-schema-v2 and is visible on the onboarding dashboard with links to the perf-run and conversion logs.
End-to-end flow has an automated rollback path if smoke-suite fails with clear failure reasons surfaced in the runbook.
Security checklist completed: manifest signing, provenance fields, and KMS-encrypted transfer for restricted uploads when requested.

notes: This ticket is intentionally opinionated: translator produces a single canonical bundle + conversion hash to make pinning deterministic. The empirical profile is minimal at first — P50/P95 and tokens/sec — but should be extensible to include regression evals later. Keep the UX flow fast (target < 30 minutes for small-weights admission) so the PM/solutions team can iterate with community models.
